quote.text: Act in this way regarding spouses, children, honors, offices, and wealth, and you will become worthy to feast with the gods. More than this—if you abstain from the rich desserts that come your way, passing them on to others, you will become worthy to rule with the gods. This was the way of Diogenes and Heraclitus, and they are now venerated as divine.
quote.author: Epictetus
quote.aiInsight:
• Parenthood
    • Emulate self-restraint with your children by modeling a life of simplicity and virtue; like Epictetus urges, steering away from excess helps shape their moral character.
    • Foster an environment where values are passed down generously, teaching them that true fulfillment arises from meaningful actions rather than pursuit of material indulgence.
  • Leadership
    • Lead with integrity by placing service above personal gain; embody the wisdom that true leadership is earned through disciplined restraint and selfless action.
    • Recognize that the honor of leadership comes not from titles or wealth, but from the willingness to forgo lavish rewards for the betterment of your community.
  • Product Management
    • Apply the principle of moderation by focusing on sustainable value—prioritize features and processes that truly benefit your users over superficial embellishments.
    • Just as divine virtue elevates a leader, cultivate transparency and generosity in sharing insights and successes with your team to create a collaborative, ethical workplace.
